title: Interior acts differ easily from divine worship; exterior signs mostly do not, except sacrifice
source_text: IV. Caeterum honorem illum quem Sanctis deberi contendunt, a divino quoad actus internos multum distare, & facile distingui posse: non item vero quoad actus externos, & externa cultus & honoris signa, quae pleraque communiter in cultu Dei & Sanctorum adhibent, excepto sacrificio, & quae ad sacrificium proprie referuntur, qualia sunt arae, templa, sacerdotes.
pass_a_gloss: But that honor which they contend is owed to the Saints stands far from the divine honor as to interior acts, and can easily be distinguished: not so, however, as to exterior acts and the outward signs of cult and honor, most of which they commonly use in the cult of God and of the Saints, except sacrifice and the things properly referred to sacrifice, such as altars, temples, and priests.
pass_b_english: On Rome's account, inward acts of Saint-honor are easy to tell apart from inward worship of God.
Outward signs are mostly shared by both cults.
The stated exception is sacrifice, together with altars, temples, and priests that belong to it.

choices.why: These are the exterior items Rome itself ties to sacrifice rather than to dulia.
